Regular shift minutes
The safety meeting began this evening

Attendees were Hugo Bennett, Talia Lee, and Maggie.

The group reviewed routine desk coverage and agreed the Companion Animal Travel Desk should keep its usual calm pace even when the queue builds. Staff noted that clear checks on carrier fit, harness use, and paperwork help cut down on last minute stress for travelers and pets alike. The tone at the counter was praised as friendly and steady, with a reminder that a warm start usually keeps the rest of the process smooth. Safety still came first on every journey, and everyone backed the habit of slowing down when a detail looks uncertain.

Discussion also covered common traveler questions about feeding breaks, water access, and comfort during transfer waits. The desk agreed to answer plainly and avoid jargon, since most people just want quick reassurance and a simple next step. There was a brief note on pets that arrive nervous, with Maggie mentioned as a good reminder that a quiet voice and an unhurried hand can settle things fast. The team also agreed that a tidy counter and checked supplies make the whole desk look more reliable to passengers.

One final point was that staff should keep passing along unusual travel concerns early, so support can be arranged before boarding becomes hectic. The meeting ended with a shared reminder that careful service protects both animal welfare and the Aurelia Skyways experience.
